question_text: If there are multiple README files, which of the following locations will be displayed first?

comments.author: Deequation
comments.text:
While the answer 'root' makes sense from the old days. Now days, the .github folder is used to store a lot of the markdown files, that makes up a repository, and these actually take priority, over files located in the root. I had to try this out myself - and it absolutely does use the file in .github. The documentation, which you can easily find, says the following:
"If a repository contains more than one README file, then the file shown is chosen from locations in the following order: the .github directory, then the repository's root directory, and finally the docs directory."
Let this be a good reminder, to structure your repositories better, and get rid of all the markdown files from the root.

comments.author: ETU69
comments.text: Yes. Correct. Did the test myself as well.

comments.author: santa3456
comments.text:
When a repository contains multiple README files in different locations, the file displayed first is chosen based on a specific order of precedence.
This order is as follows:
.github directory: A README file located within the .github directory takes the highest precedence.
Repository's root directory: If no README is found in .github, the system will then look for a README in the main root directory of the repository.
docs directory: If no README is found in either of the above locations, the system will finally check the docs directory for a README file.

comments.author: PawanDev
comments.text:
In GitHub, when a repository is displayed, the README file shown on the main page is the one located in the root of the repository.
README files in subfolders like docs, src, or .github are not displayed by default on the main repository page; they are only shown when navigating to that folder.

comments.author: Vikram1710
comments.text: It should be Root

opening a pull request or issue
being assigned to an issue or pull request

comments.author: Kiwi28
comments.text:
The correct answers are C, D, and E. ✅
GitHub’s official documentation says you are automatically subscribed to a conversation when you:
- C. open a pull request or issue ✅
- D. are assigned to an issue or pull request ✅

- D. default editor ✅ — you can choose whether Codespaces opens in VS Code web, VS Code desktop, or JupyterLab. GitHub Docs

- F. API Keys ✅
